dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to scaffold local memory/reference/state layouts, and the bundled scripts match that purpose by creating missing folders, seed indexes, reference stubs, and topic index entries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly discloses workspace inspection and local writes, requires dry-run review and human approval before applying scaffold changes, and forbids deleting, renaming, bulk overwriting, or storing secrets; however, one stub-writing helper writes to the exact --out path and should be used only for new or intentionally replaced files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is ordinary ClawHub npx guidance and the artifacts show no post-install hooks, hidden downloads, automatic execution, or installer-time mutation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local file read/write capability is proportionate for a filesystem scaffolding skill; the scripts use user-supplied paths, do not invoke shells, and contain no network, credential, browser-profile, or session-store access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally creates durable local folders, indexes, reference stubs, and an appended setup log, but does not create background workers, privilege escalation, autostart entries, or unbounded persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The filesystem read/write behavior is real, but it is the core disclosed purpose of the skill and is bounded by user-chosen paths, dry-run review, additive scaffolding, and explicit no-delete/no-secret instructions.
[SDI-1] expected: The examples include state index maintenance and helper script usage, but those scripts are bundled, simple, local filesystem utilities aligned with the skill's documented workflow rather than hidden operational expansion.
[SDI-2] expected: The command examples are disclosed and purpose-aligned; the optional lyra-brain handoff broadens the workflow, but it is labeled as a paired optional step and not automatic execution.
llm.guidance: Install this only if you want an agent to help organize a local workspace into memory/reference/state folders. Review the dry-run plan before allowing writes, use explicit workspace paths, avoid storing secrets in generated notes or stubs, and require separate approval before running optional paired lyra-brain or lattice helper commands.
llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed local filesystem helper that creates and updates memory/reference files, with no evidence of network exfiltration, hidden persistence, or destructive behavior.
